info.bio:
Jim Steinman cuyo nombre real es James Richard Steinman (nacido en Noviembre 1 de 1947, New York) es un productor, compositor y cantautor americano. Él es el responsable de éxitos musicales como "Total Eclipse Of The Heart", de Bonnie Tyler, "Making Love (Out Of Nothing At All), de Air Supply, y "I'd Do Anything for Love (but I Won't Do That)", de Meat Loaf (entre otros).

Empezó su carrera en teatro; su trabajo más notable es con las letras del musical "Whistle Down the Wind" y "Tanz der Vampire".

scenes.name: Techno-rock y pop de estudio
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El «sonido» por encima de la melodía, el ritmo y la armonía: Electric Light Orchestra inventa el «high-tech pop»; Supertramp, Alan Parsons Project, Kansas, Styx y Split Enz. El valor de la producción define a Steely Dan (el pop-jazz pulido de los yuppies), Hall & Oates, los Fleetwood Mac de Rumours y Tusk, Toto, el «muro de sonido» titánico de Jim Steinman (Bat Out Of Hell) y la Penguin Cafe Orchestra. A finales de los setenta, el art-rock culmina en los supergrupos: 10cc, Godley & Creme, Foreigner, UK, Asia, Sky.

scenes.name: College-pop y nacimiento del lo-fi
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La población universitaria del Sur adopta la ética de la new wave y la adapta a la melodía: un pop inusualmente intelectual, con raíces en el folk-rock y el country-rock pero contaminado por las neurosis de la época. Athens (Georgia) compite con las capitales del rock: B-52's y R.E.M., uno de los grupos de más éxito de la historia. Carolina del Norte (dB's, Windbreakers), Hoboken (Smithereens, Bongos, Tiny Lights), el nacimiento del lo-fi (Half Japanese, Violent Femmes, Beat Happening, Guided By Voices, Sebadoh), They Might Be Giants, Green, B.A.L.L., Boston (Volcano Suns, 10,000 Maniacs, Throwing Muses, Blake Babies), la Costa Oeste (Game Theory, Posies, Young Fresh Fellows) y la sátira de Ween.

podcast.title: "More Than You Deserve" Musical (1973)
podcast.body: Jim Steinman's 1973 musical, "More Than You Deserve," was where he first met Meat Loaf when the latter auditioned. Many of the songs that would later appear on *Bat Out of Hell* were developed or conceived during this period, particularly during the National Lampoon tour that Ellen Foley and Meat Loaf participated in. "He met Steinman in the early 70s when he auditioned for Steinman's 1973 musical More Than You Deserve."

podcast.title: Clive Davis Rejection and Critique
podcast.body: Clive Davis, the head of CBS Records, famously refused to produce *Bat Out of Hell*, stating bluntly to Jim Steinman, "clearly you have no idea how to write a rock song." This harsh critique came despite Steinman's unique blend of theatrical and rock influences. "CBS Records, which was run by the legendary Clive Davis, said via Clive Davis that, no way, be making this. In fact, Clive Davis told Jim Steinman, clearly you have no idea how to write a rock song."

podcast.title: Musical Influences
podcast.body: Jim Steinman, writer of the songs on *Bat Out of Hell*, was heavily influenced by both Wagnerian opera and early rock and roll artists such as Little Richard and Jerry Lee Lewis. As a child, he would follow opera listening sessions with these rock pioneers. "The songs were written by Jim Steinman, who was heavily influenced by Wagner, but he also loved rock and roll. So as a kid, he would listen to some opera, and then he would follow that up as one does, with some little Richard or Jerry Lee Lewis."

podcast.title: Teenage Desires as Inspiration
podcast.body: Ellen Foley, the female vocalist on "Paradise by the Dashboard Light," suggested that Jim Steinman's "hyper-emotional material" for *Bat Out of Hell* was likely him "working out his own teenage desires that he hadn't done in real life." He aimed to create something entirely unprecedented in music. "I don't want to be a shrink, but I think it was probably him working out his own teenage desires that he hadn't done in real life, but was able to experience in this hyper-emotional material. He just wanted to create something that nobody had ever heard before."
